e: Validation checks a rule or format; verification checks data matches the original/source input.
Give a suitable boundary value when valid ages are 13–18. [2 marks]
13 or 18, plus an adjacent invalid such as 12 or 19 for a test set.
State one difference between authentication and validation. [2 marks]
Authentication confirms an asserted identity; validation checks input against constraints.

r: Correct: 'ROM loses its data when power is removed'.
ROM is non-volatile; contents remain without power.
Explain why opening a file in the wrong mode can cause a problem.
Write mode may overwrite data; read mode may prevent updates, depending on the system.
State the difference between RAM and ROM.
RAM is volatile working memory; ROM stores persistent firmware.
Explain the prerequisite for binary search and why it matters.
The list must be sorted so midpoint comparisons can safely discard one half.

stretch.task: Modify the program to accept ages 13–18 rather than marks 0–100. Check 12, 13, 18 and 19.

mastery.task: Write a loop that continues asking for a score until an integer in 0–100 is provided. Specify expected results for text input and for both numeric boundaries.
mastery.hint: Validation is not complete when ELSE only prints 'Invalid'—it must ask again.
mastery.answer: Use a repeat-until-valid structure; reject wrong-type input safely before numerical comparison; accept 0 and 100; reject -1, 101 and 'cat'. This extends the starting range check rather than requiring a totally new concept.
